//! Server-Sent Events (SSE) Handler

use axum::{
    extract::Extension,
    response::sse::{Event, Sse},
};
use futures::stream::{self, Stream};
use std::convert::Infallible;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Duration;
use tokio::sync::broadcast;
use tokio_stream::wrappers::BroadcastStream;
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;

use crate::state::AppState;

/// SSE Event Broadcaster
pub struct SseEventBroadcaster {
    tx: broadcast::Sender<SseEvent>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct SseEvent {
    pub event_type: String,
    pub data: String,
}

impl Default for SseEventBroadcaster {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl SseEventBroadcaster {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        // Sized for a hydration burst, not for steady state: on connect the
        // upstream sends one contract and one state frame per plugin back to
        // back. At 100 a browser that reads slowly would silently lose part of
        // its own hydration, and dropped state frames — unlike dropped schema
        // frames — leave no trace a consumer can detect.
        let (tx, _) = broadcast::channel(1024);
        Self { tx }
    }

    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub fn broadcast(&self, event_type: &str, data: &str) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(SseEvent {
            event_type: event_type.to_string(),
            data: data.to_string(),
        });
    }

    pub fn subscribe(&self) -> broadcast::Receiver<SseEvent> {
        self.tx.subscribe()
    }
}

/// Replayable hydration for browsers that connect after op-web did.
///
/// Hydration happens once, when *op-web* opens its upstream subscription. Every
/// browser after that attaches to a live broadcast and would otherwise see
/// nothing until something mutates — which is why a freshly opened dashboard
/// looked empty even though the system was fully populated.
///
/// So the bridge records the last frame it saw per contract and per state key,
/// and each new SSE subscriber is replayed that set before the live stream.
/// This is a replay buffer, not a second source of truth: every entry is a
/// verbatim frame the upstream produced, and the contract hashes on them let a
/// consumer detect if a replayed frame is behind the catalog.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct HydrationCache {
    /// Latest contract frame per plugin id.
    schemas: std::sync::RwLock<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, String>>,
    /// Latest state frame per `plugin|path|property` key — the same key the UI
    /// accumulates under, so a replay reconstructs exactly what a subscriber
    /// present from the start would be holding.
    states: std::sync::RwLock<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, String>>,
}

impl HydrationCache {
    pub fn record_schema(&self, plugin_id: &str, json: &str) {
        if let Ok(mut schemas) = self.schemas.write() {
            schemas.insert(plugin_id.to_string(), json.to_string());
        }
    }

    pub fn record_state(&self, key: String, json: &str) {
        if let Ok(mut states) = self.states.write() {
            states.insert(key, json.to_string());
        }
    }

    /// Contracts first, then state — a renderer needs the shape before values.
    pub fn replay(&self) -> Vec<SseEvent> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        if let Ok(schemas) = self.schemas.read() {
            out.extend(schemas.values().map(|data| SseEvent {
                event_type: "schema_update".to_string(),
                data: data.clone(),
            }));
        }
        if let Ok(states) = self.states.read() {
            out.extend(states.values().map(|data| SseEvent {
                event_type: "state_update".to_string(),
                data: data.clone(),
            }));
        }
        out
    }

    pub fn len(&self) -> (usize, usize) {
        (
            self.schemas.read().map(|s| s.len()).unwrap_or(0),
            self.states.read().map(|s| s.len()).unwrap_or(0),
        )
    }
}

/// GET /api/events - SSE event stream
pub async fn sse_handler(
    Extension(state): Extension<Arc<AppState>>,
) -> Sse<impl Stream<Item = Result<Event, Infallible>>> {
    // Subscribe before taking the replay so a frame arriving mid-hydration is
    // duplicated rather than lost. Same ordering rule the gRPC subscribe uses.
    let rx = state.sse_broadcaster.subscribe();
    let replay = state.hydration.replay();

    let stream = BroadcastStream::new(rx).filter_map(
        |result: Result<SseEvent, tokio_stream::wrappers::errors::BroadcastStreamRecvError>| {
            result
                .ok()
                .map(|event| Ok(Event::default().event(event.event_type).data(event.data)))
        },
    );

    // Replay is ordered and must arrive before anything live, so it is chained
    // ahead of the broadcast rather than selected against it.
    let hydration = stream::iter(
        replay
            .into_iter()
            .map(|event| Ok(Event::default().event(event.event_type).data(event.data))),
    );
    let stream = hydration.chain(stream);

    // Add keepalive
    let keepalive = stream::repeat_with(|| Ok(Event::default().comment("keepalive")))
        .throttle(Duration::from_secs(30));

    let combined = stream::select(stream, keepalive);

    Sse::new(combined).keep_alive(
        axum::response::sse::KeepAlive::new()
            .interval(Duration::from_secs(15))
            .text("ping"),
    )
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn replay_puts_every_contract_before_any_state() {
        let cache = HydrationCache::default();
        cache.record_state("network|/p/network|bridges".into(), r#"{"v":1}"#);
        cache.record_schema("network", r#"{"schema_hash":"aaaa"}"#);
        cache.record_state("adc|/p/adc|status".into(), r#"{"v":2}"#);
        cache.record_schema("adc", r#"{"schema_hash":"bbbb"}"#);

        let replay = cache.replay();
        let kinds: Vec<&str> = replay.iter().map(|e| e.event_type.as_str()).collect();

        // A renderer needs the shape before the values, regardless of the order
        // the frames were originally recorded in.
        assert_eq!(
            kinds,
            vec![
                "schema_update",
                "schema_update",
                "state_update",
                "state_update"
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(cache.len(), (2, 2));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_replaced_frame_is_not_replayed_twice() {
        let cache = HydrationCache::default();
        cache.record_schema("network", r#"{"schema_hash":"old"}"#);
        cache.record_schema("network", r#"{"schema_hash":"new"}"#);

# Complete Antigravity Data Flow: StateSync → Dashboard

## Overview
Antigravity data flows from a Rust backend StateSync service through a gRPC bridge into op-web, which broadcasts it as Server-Sent Events (SSE) to the dashboard frontend. The frontend decodes this stream into React state, which is then rendered by component trees.

---

## 1. Decoding: How Data is Parsed (`dashboard-stream.ts`)

**Entry Point:** `parseDashboardStreamEvent()` at line 156

The dashboard receives raw JSON from the SSE stream and decodes it through this pipeline:

```
Raw SSE String → JSON parse → Type detection → DashboardStreamEvent
```

### Key Decoding Steps:

1. **JSON Parsing** (lines 156-170): Raw string is parsed into a typed `DashboardEventPayload` union:
   - `StateUpdatePayload` - plugin state changes with metadata (plugin_id, object_path, property_name, old_value, new_value, event_hash, catalog_hash, frame_kind)
   - `SchemaUpdatePayload` - contract definition frames (contains schema hash and full contract in new_value)
   - `AuditEventPayload` - snowball audit trail entries
   - `SystemStatsPayload` - uptime/memory/CPU metrics
   - `UnknownEventPayload` - fallback for parse errors

2. **Type Classification** (lines 150-154): Event type string is normalized against known types. Unknown types default to "unknown".

3. **Reception Timestamp** (line 168): `receivedAt: Date.now()` captures client-side arrival time.

### Schema Detection (lines 172-181):
Frames are checked for stale contracts — if a state frame cites a schema hash not yet held by the client, the plugin is marked as stale. This is the **only observable trace** of a dropped schema frame on the stream (line 171 comment).

---

## 2. State Storage (`useDashboardEventStream.ts` hook + Redux-like reducer)

**Entry Point:** `useDashboardEventStream()` at line 16

This React hook manages the full lifecycle:

### Hook Initialization (lines 20-26):
- Creates initial `DashboardStreamState` (line 22): empty events array, empty keyed state, no schemas, no stale plugins
- Connects to `${API_BASE}/events` SSE endpoint (line 30)

### Event Subscription (lines 33-38):
- Registers listeners for each event type: `state_update`, `schema_update`, `audit_event`, `system_stats`
- Generic message handler also routes to `"message"` type for untyped events
- Each event flows through `reduceDashboardStreamEvent()` (line 36)

### State Accumulation (`reduceDashboardStreamEvent()` in dashboard-stream.ts, lines 196-266):

**For state_update events** (lines 204-218):
- **Heartbeats** (frame_kind="heartbeat"): No keying, only updates catalogHash
- **Real updates**: Stored by key = `"${plugin_id}:${object_path}:${property_name}"`
- **Schema staleness tracking**: If frame cites unknown schema, plugin added to `staleSchemas[]`

**For schema_update events** (lines 220-233):
- Schema stored by plugin_id in `schemasByPlugin` map
- Receiving a schema clears staleness for that plugin
- Each new schema replaces the old one (not accumulated)

**For audit/stats events** (lines 235-245):
- Audit events stored as `lastAuditEvent`
- System stats stored as `latestSystemStats`

**Rate limiting** (line 200): Events array capped at `MAX_STREAM_EVENTS` (40 events), older events dropped

**Usage counters** (line 201): Per-event-type counts incremented

The resulting `DashboardStreamState` holds:
- `connected: boolean` - SSE connection status
- `latestStateByKey: Record<string, StateUpdatePayload>` - present state of all plugins
- `schemasByPlugin: Record<string, SchemaUpdatePayload>` - schema definitions
- `catalogHash: string` - current contract catalog identity
- `staleSchemas: string[]` - plugins missing their schema
- `latestSystemStats` / `lastAuditEvent` - singleton latest

---

## 3. Rendering in the Dashboard

### Component Tree Entry (`App.tsx`, line 29):
The router mounts pages that consume stream state. Example: `StatePage.tsx`

### StatePage Example Rendering (lines 21-120):
- **Data source**: Mock data hardcoded, but pattern shows how live data would be consumed
- Uses `Tabs` component to show two surfaces:
  1. **Snowball tab**: Shows audit trail (uses `lastAuditEvent` from stream state)
  2. **State tab**: Shows state entries (would use `latestStateByKey` keyed entries)

### JsonRenderView Component (`JsonRenderView.tsx`):
Generic renderer for streaming UI specs:
```typescript
<JSONUIProvider
  registry={registry}
  initialState={state}
  handlers={handlers}
/>
```
- Accepts a `Spec` (UI structure definition)
- Binds `initialState` from stream state
- Renders components dynamically per spec

### Real-time Reactivity:
```typescript
export function useDashboardEventStream() {
  const [state, setState] = useState<DashboardStreamState>(() =>
    createInitialDashboardStreamState(),
  );
  // ...
  setState((current) =>
    reduceDashboardStreamEvent(
      current,
      parseDashboardStreamEvent(eventType, event.data),
    ),
  );
  // ...
  return useMemo(() => state, [state]);
}
```
Each SSE event → `parseDashboardStreamEvent()` → `reduceDashboardStreamEvent()` → `setState()` → component re-render

---

## 4. Backend: From Antigravity Through op-web

### Rust Plugin State (`antigravity.rs`):
- `AntigravityState` struct (line 318) defines the full schema
- `AntigravityPlugin::current_state()` (line 458) reads environment and returns hydrated state
- Serialized to JSON and published to StateSync

### SSE Broadcaster & Hydration (`sse.rs`):

**Hydration Cache** (lines 67-115):
- Stores the latest frame per plugin (contracts) and per state key (values)
- Contracts replayed first, then states (line 111) — renderer needs schema before values
- On each new browser connection, entire cache is replayed, then live stream begins

**SSE Handler** (lines 119-148):
```rust
pub async fn sse_handler(...) -> Sse<impl Stream> {
  let rx = state.sse_broadcaster.subscribe();  // Subscribe first
  let replay = state.hydration.replay();        // Then replay
  // Chain: replay buffer → live broadcast → keepalive (every 30s)
}
```

### Frame Flow Path:
1. StateSync upstream generates `StateUpdatePayload` / `SchemaUpdatePayload` frames
2. op-web records in `HydrationCache` (plugin_id + json string for schema, key + json for state)
3. Frames broadcast via `SseEventBroadcaster` (lines 19-60)
4. Browser SSE connection receives frames, calls event listeners registered in `useDashboardEventStream.ts`
5. Each frame decoded, reduced into React state, triggers re-render

---

## Key Data Structures

### On the Wire (SSE frame):
```typescript
{
  type: "state_update",                // Event type
  receivedAt: 1708104721234,          // Client timestamp
  payload: {
    plugin_id: "antigravity",
    object_path: "/plugins/antigravity",
    property_name: "status",
    new_value: { mode: "active" },
    schema_hash: "held_by_client",     // Matches schemasByPlugin[plugin_id].schema_hash
    catalog_hash: "cat-v2",            // Identity of contract catalog
    change_type: "property_set",
    frame_kind: "update"               // "initial_state", "update", or "heartbeat"
  }
}
```

### In React State:
```typescript
{
  latestStateByKey: {
    "antigravity:/plugins/antigravity:status": { ... payload ...}
  },
  schemasByPlugin: {
    "antigravity": { schema_hash: "held_by_client", new_value: {...contract...} }
  },
  staleSchemas: [],  // Empty if all cited schemas are held
  catalogHash: "cat-v2"
}
```

---

## Critical Behaviors

1. **Schema Staleness Detection** (lines 171-181, 220-233): If a state frame cites a schema_hash not in `schemasByPlugin`, the plugin is flagged as stale. This signals that a schema frame was dropped. Consumers can detect drift without retrying — the hash mismatch is the only trace.

2. **Hydration Ordering** (sse.rs line 111): Contracts always replay before state. This ensures renderers never try to render values against an unknown schema.

3. **Keepalive Strategy** (sse.rs line 146): 30-second repeating keepalive comments prevent idle connection closes. Each frame carries `catalogHash`, so an idle stream still reveals if contracts moved.

4. **Rate Limiting** (line 200): Event array capped at 40 to prevent unbounded growth. Old events are dropped; only latest state per key is accumulated.

5. **No Double Replay** (sse.rs test line 215): If a frame arrives twice (e.g., one in replay + one live), only the latest is held. The cache deduplicates by key.
